title: Prevent path traversal in a file viewer
description: Resolve a requested filename and ensure it stays inside an approved folder.
code:
from pathlib import Path
BASE = Path("user-files").resolve()
def safe_file(name):
    candidate = (BASE / name).resolve()
    if candidate != BASE and BASE not in candidate.parents:
        raise ValueError("Path is outside the permitted folder")
    return candidate

print(safe_file("notes.txt"))

title: Use parameterized SQLite queries
description: Use placeholders rather than string concatenation for SQL values.
code:
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE users (username TEXT)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?)", ("ram",))
requested = "ram' OR '1'='1"
rows = db.execute(
    "SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = ?",
    (requested,)
).fetchall()
print(rows)  # No SQL syntax is injected

title: Create a safe server-side upload filename
description: Generate a random storage name instead of trusting a user-supplied filename.
code:
import secrets
from pathlib import Path
def safe_upload_name(original_name):
    suffix = Path(original_name).suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in {".png", ".jpg", ".pdf"}:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported file type")
    return secrets.token_hex(16) + suffix

print(safe_upload_name("my-photo.png"))

title: Hash a password with scrypt
description: Use a password-hashing function rather than a fast general-purpose hash.
code:
import os, hashlib
password = b"example-only-password"
salt = os.urandom(16)
digest = hashlib.scrypt(password, salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
print("salt:", salt.hex())
print("hash:", digest.hex())

title: Verify a scrypt password hash
description: Recompute the hash using the stored salt and compare in constant time.
code:
import hashlib, hmac
def verify_scrypt(password, salt, expected):
    actual = hashlib.scrypt(password, salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
    return hmac.compare_digest(actual, expected)

salt = b"0123456789abcdef"
saved = hashlib.scrypt(b"demo-password", salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
print(verify_scrypt(b"demo-password", salt, saved))

title: Apply login rate limiting in a toy example
description: Demonstrate a per-account attempt counter; use a shared store and careful lockout policy in production.
code:
from collections import defaultdict
attempts = defaultdict(int)
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
def allow_login_attempt(account):
    attempts[account] += 1
    return attempts[account] <= MAX_ATTEMPTS

for _ in range(6):
    print(allow_login_attempt("demo-user"))

title: Validate a redirect destination
description: Allow only relative paths to avoid sending users to arbitrary external destinations.
code:
from urllib.parse import urlparse
def safe_redirect(target):
    parsed = urlparse(target)
    if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc or not target.startswith("/") or target.startswith("//"):
        raise ValueError("Redirect destination not allowed")
    return target

print(safe_redirect("/dashboard"))
